name: Lit ridge near Shackleton (computed)
source: Lit member of a lit/dark pair about 2100 m apart, re-found with a finer scan (50 m grid) by the repick scripts using the 2 m observer; about 7936 h of Sun in 2027. Positions scanned on LRO LOLA DEM v4 S Pole (5 m, 87.5 deg, NASA Moon Trek) with a 2 m observer height; Sun and Earth hours are for 2027.

name: IM-2 landing site, Mons Mouton
source: Intuitive Machines IM-2 intended landing site, as published by the LROC team (Robinson, 26 Feb 2025, https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1401): 84.78 S, 29.13 E. Elevation sampled from LRO LOLA DEM v4 S Pole (30 m, 75 deg, NASA Moon Trek) with a 2 m observer height; Sun and Earth hours are for 2027.

name: Haworth region centre
note: Centre of NASA's Haworth region (15 km x 15 km). The centre is on the shadowed crater floor: the horizon is never below 3.7 deg and the Sun peaks at 4.1 deg, so it gets 0 h of Sun in 2027 (Earth is visible part of the time). A scan of the whole region on a 250 m grid found no lit point.
source: Centre point of the NASA Artemis III candidate region Haworth, as listed on the Lunar Resources Registry south pole map (https://lunarresourcesregistry.com/south-pole-map/, a third-party map of NASA's regions): 87.45 S, 5.0 W. Elevation sampled from LRO LOLA DEM v4 S Pole (30 m, 75 deg, NASA Moon Trek) with a 2 m observer height; Sun and Earth hours are for 2027 (a scan of the whole region around the centre, about 15 km x 15 km on a 500 m grid, found no point with any Sun in 2027).

name: Best-lit point on Connecting Ridge (computed)
source: Best-lit point found by scanning within about 6 km of the registry centre of the Connecting Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache, -89.45, -136.0 (Lunar Resources Registry south pole map, https://lunarresourcesregistry.com/south-pole-map/, a third-party map of NASA's 2022 candidate regions), on LRO LOLA DEM v4 S Pole (5 m, 87.5 deg, NASA Moon Trek) with a 2 m observer height; Sun and Earth hours are for 2027. Kept as a plausibility check against Glaser et al. 2014 (Icarus 243, 78, https://elib.dlr.de/94242), who report this ridge about 92% sunlit at 2 m over 19 years; their exact point is unknown, so this is not a replication.
